sec: Seroconversion before immunosuppression, clinical features, extrahepatic disease, replicative load

items.q: Fill up (Seroconversion): 'Both markers should be checked before ______ therapy.'
items.exp: 'Seroconversion : Both markers should be checked before immunosuppressive therapy.' (Book p1041)

items.q: Match the two markers the page asks for — 1) First marker 2) Second marker … A) Anti-HBc IgG B) HBsAg
items.exp: The pair printed before immunosuppressive therapy is HBsAg and anti-HBc IgG. (Book p1041)

items.q: Before immunosuppression, screening shows HBsAg negative but anti-HBc IgG positive. What does this page warn about?
opts: No risk at all, because HBsAg is negative
Acute hepatitis B that needs vaccination
items.exp: HBsAg -ve with anti-HBc IgG +ve is the pattern arrowed to 'Immunosuppressive therapy → Reactivation'. (Book p1041)

items.q: Judge the seroconversion block: I HBsAg negative with anti-HBc IgG negative is the pattern with no reactivation risk. II HBsAg negative with anti-HBc IgG positive is the carrier pattern that reactivates on immunosuppression.
items.exp: Two patterns are contrasted: both markers negative, versus HBsAg -ve with anti-HBc IgG +ve, the latter running into reactivation. (Book p1041)

items.q: Clinical features — match — 1) Acute hepatitis column 2) Chronic hepatitis column … A) Asymptomatic presentation, fatigue (most common symptom), fever, extrahepatic manifestations B) Acute hepatitis B, reactivation
items.exp: 'Clinical Features' splits into Acute hepatitis (Acute hepatitis B, Reactivation) and Chronic hepatitis (Asymptomatic presentation, Fatigue — most common symptom, Fever, Extrahepatic manifestation). (Book p1041)

items.q: Which symptom does the page print as the most common symptom of chronic hepatitis B?
Which is NOT one of the rare extrahepatic manifestations listed for chronic hepatitis B?
items.exp: 'Extrahepatic manifestation (Rare) : membranous nephropathy, Polyarteritis Nodosa (30%), Arthralgia'. (Book p1041)

items.q: What figure is printed alongside polyarteritis nodosa in the extrahepatic list?
Which investigation is printed next to 'Cirrhosis' in the work-up line?
The 'Replicative load' section is divided into which two branches?
items.exp: Two branches are drawn under 'Replicative load': 'Low Replicative' and 'High Replicative'. (Book p1041)

items.q: Replicative profiles — match — 1) HBV DNA > 20,000 IU/mL 2) HBV DNA > 2,000 IU/mL … A) HBeAg -ve (precore mutation) B) HBeAg +ve
items.exp: 'HBeAg +ve : · HBV DNA > 20,000 IU/mL'; 'HBeAg -ve (Precore mutation) : · HBV DNA > 2,000 IU/mL'. (Book p1041)

items.q: Match the profile to its printed consequences — 1) HBeAg +ve profile 2) HBeAg -ve precore-mutant profile … A) Anti-HBc reactive, progressive liver injury, bad prognosis B) High infectivity, risk of liver injury
items.exp: HBeAg +ve profile: 'High infectivity · Risk of liver injury'. Precore-mutant profile: '· Anti-HBc reactive · Progressive liver injury · Bad prognosis'. (Book p1041)

items.q: A patient with chronic HBV is HBeAg negative with HBV DNA 3,000 IU/mL. Which printed profile and consequence set applies?
opts: HBeAg -ve precore mutation — anti-HBc reactive, progressive liver injury, bad prognosis
HBeAg +ve — high infectivity, risk of liver injury
Inactive carrier — no treatment and no follow-up
Acute hepatitis B — anti-HBc IgM positive
items.exp: HBeAg -ve with DNA above 2,000 fits the 'HBeAg -ve (Precore mutation)' profile with progressive liver injury and bad prognosis. (Book p1041)

items.q: Which statement is NOT printed for the HBeAg-negative precore-mutant profile?
items.exp: 'High infectivity' belongs to the HBeAg-positive profile; the precore-mutant profile lists anti-HBc reactive, progressive liver injury and bad prognosis. (Book p1041)
